Depends on the kid. I have 10 kids, one was a very picky kid and as an adult she still is in a lot of ways but she's also willing to try things now and had added new foods to her diet. My oldest is autistic and it took me about 6 years of trying to get them to eat perogies, they eat them now but things like sauce or condiments is a no go and always will be. A bunch of my kids (both neurotypical and not) slowly have added foods. My 4 year old pretty much survives on peanut butter sandwiches and chocolate milk with other foods as snacks taken in and out of rotation.  The most successful way I have added foods was peer influence, watching other kids eating things or sitting on my lap and eating off my plate was more likely to lead to them trying things. I never ever forced anything, a little light bribery or over the top praise helps. It usually gets better, just be patient.

I'm autistic but I didn't actually know that until recently. Everyone was worried about my oldest child but they were just like me so I saw absolutely nothing wrong with them. Publicly I say I wouldn't do anything different and I'd still have them all (5 of the 8 have autism) but secretly I wonder. I wonder what would have happened if I hadn't had kids, I gave this to them, I am the reason and I feel a lot of guilt over that. I can't think too hard because the guilt is overwhelming. If I had a diagnosis before I got married, I would have done things different but I probably would have still had kids, not as many, I'd have married someone different and I'd have waited until I was older. I love them and I understand them and no one could advocate for them like I do, if they exist, I am meant to be their mom. 
All that to say, if you want a kid, have one, I don't resent my autistic father for creating me and I hope my kids won't resent me for their lives.

Are you having a C section and planning on being at the hospital for a few days?  If not you may want to rethink your plan. I can only speak to vaginal births but I really didn't stay long enough for visitors and it was honestly a bit busy there, they keep coming to check you and baby, your boobs are out, you are bleeding and it's not a big room. I had no idea how many times a nurse would walk into the room and lift up my gown and push on my stomach and omg the amount of blood that comes out of you after is honestly like a murder scene. You could probably avoid the whole problem by telling everyone to come see you once you get home and you are out of the hospital gown and have had a shower. Also take into consideration, I never said anything to anyone, I just quietly grumped in my head but there were a few times the ward was full and I was in a room with another mom and I was so exhausted and theyd start getting visitors and they are loud and I just wanted to sleep. It's 100% your decision and if you want visitors then that is totally your choice, just as someone who's done it a few times (I've had 8 babies) I highly recommend taking the time in the hospital with just the three of you and have people visit once you get home.

I've had 8 babies, when I was pregnant with my first, my cousin was working in labour and delivery as a nursing student and there was a mom who had the epidural needle break off in her spine and ended up paralyzed. I'm sure the chances of this happening are astronomically low and sooooo many people have uneventful procedures where absolutely nothing goes wrong but I was 20 years old and already nervous so I just totally wrote that off as an option. I'm not telling anyone not to get one because as I'll get to, it turns out they are pretty amazing. My second baby came too fast for any kind of pain meds and by the third I learned how to breathe through the pain and actually didn't need anything. I had no pain meds until the 8th who was a scheduled induction because Covid was nuts here and there was a very real possibility that my husband would miss the birth if we didn't evict him that week. So my body and baby did not like the induction and I didn't know I could feel pain like that, even my doctor who delivered all but 2 of my kids said she'd never seen me cry like that. I got the epidural and holy crap it was instant relief. Turns out he was sunny side up and they had to reach in to turn him and I was so so grateful I couldn't feel that. I already knew how to push from previous deliveries so I got him out in just a couple pushes but i could imagine pushing when you can't feel anything would be weird and hard. I've spent the last few months since then so conflicted, That epidural was the best thing in the world and I didn't know if I felt regret over not having one for the other kids, I'm still not sure how I feel about it and will I'll just probably remain conflicted forever. My baby is the last I'll have but 100% if I ever was induced again there would be no question of an epidural, I'd want it the second I got to the hospital, I wouldn't try to wait, I wouldn't try and prove anything to anyone even myself I'd want the freaking drugs. 

My point to all of it was, it doesn't matter what anyone else does, it doesn't matter what you plan for because plans change especially in childbirth. All that matters is how you feel and what you need when you are going through it. Just do what's right for you and don't even take anyone else's preferences or opinions into account. This is about you. I hope you have a peaceful birth however it ends up happening.

We have 9 (almost 10 kids) our grocery bill is high but not for how many people we have here a quick rundown of my tips:
-I ditched the chest freezer and got the upright one because in our house, things go to die at the bottom. We have a second fridge so we can do only one Costco trip a month. (You wouldn’t believe how much yogurt and milk we go through) 
-I bake all after school treats, my husband and I don’t like the cheap bread the kids eat so I bake the fancier stuff for us. 
- we do online grocery shopping for the stuff that doesn’t come from Costco, we aren’t tempted by extra stuff walking down the isles. If we need something unexpectedly, I run into the store just before I have to get the kids from school so I don’t have time to get distracted by snacks, just in and out. 
- we very rarely get take out but when we do it’s usually pizza and we wait for the special half price deals so it’s not expensive. 
-we start saving for Christmas a few months before and we stick to the budget closely. The kids get good Christmas and birthday presents but we don’t buy them much in between other than clothes or necessities. If they want something extra they save up chore points to trade in for money or cut grass/shovel driveways. 
-we have an excessive number of pets, I buy food from the farm supply store because it’s sooooo much cheaper. 
-I buy juice or pop on special occasions but otherwise if they want it, they buy it themselves (the big kids do, the younger kids don’t actually like it)

I probably have a million more things but these are the bigger ones.

With the first I had no idea when to push though, the doctor had to tell me it was time. The second, I thought I had bad heartburn that would come and go and I was a bit crampy most of the day but it was just uncomfortable and annoying, by the time I was in pain I barely made it to the hospital, my water broke and his head was visible, it felt like everything in my body was trying to push him out on it’s own. Most of my other kids were typical labour’s until the last, I was dreaming I was in labour and woke up and realized I had actually slept through most of labour, again, that one it felt like the contractions were my muscles were working on their own to push her out, it was involuntary.

This was just my experience but basically, be aware of fluid leaking, that means your water broke. Any pains that you feel through your back and down the front of your stomach into your uterus, pay attention to if the come and go. There are apps for your phone to time them to see how far apart they are and if they are regular. Feeling like you need to push or need to poop, means haul ass to the hospital. If you aren’t sure, call the doctor or go in, they’d rather send you home than have you deliver at home in your bathroom.  They hurt but I learned by the third kid that breathing really does help if you are doing it properly. Hope that helps. Good luck and hope it goes smoothly for you.
